questions.q: How do we compare the Simple Present and the Present Progressive?
questions.a: Simple Present alışkanlık ve rutinleri (I study every day), Present Progressive şu an süren eylemleri (I am studying now) anlatır.

questions.q: What are adverbs of frequency and where are they placed?
questions.a: Always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never; genellikle ana fiilden önce, 'be' fiilinden sonra yer alır.

questions.q: Give examples of polite requests and offers with modals.
questions.a: Could you help me, please? / May I ask a question? / Shall we start? — kibar rica ve teklif kalıplarıdır.

questions.q: How do articles and quantifiers work in English?
questions.a: a/an belirsiz, the belirli tanımlıktır; some/any, much/many, a lot of miktar belirtir.

questions.q: What is a question tag? Give an example.
questions.a: Cümle sonuna eklenen kısa soru eki: 'You like English, don't you?'

questions.q: What expressions are used to ask for clarification in class?
questions.a: Could you repeat that, please? / What does ... mean? / Can you explain it again?

questions.q: Name different learning styles.
questions.a: Visual, auditory, kinaesthetic, reading/writing learners.

questions.q: How do we talk about study habits?
questions.a: I usually take notes. I revise every evening. I learn best by listening.

questions.q: How do we talk about health and well-being?
questions.a: Using 'should/shouldn't': You should sleep well. You shouldn't eat too much sugar.

questions.q: Name some feelings and emotions.
questions.a: Happy, sad, excited, worried, tired, relaxed, stressed, proud.

questions.q: How do we ask about hobbies and free time?
questions.a: What do you do in your free time? / I enjoy reading and playing football.

questions.q: How do we describe our home and family?
questions.a: There is/are, have got/has got ve aile üyeleri: 'We have got a big garden.' / 'My sister has got her own room.'

questions.q: Name household chores in English.
questions.a: Do the washing-up, tidy up, do the laundry, water the plants, take out the rubbish.

questions.q: How do we express possession?
questions.a: Possessive 's ve iyelik sıfatları: my, your, his, her, our, their; 'my mother's car'.

units.name: Theme 5 - Life in the Neighbourhood, City & Social Life

questions.q: How do we ask for and give directions?
questions.a: Excuse me, how can I get to ...? Go straight, turn left at the corner, it's next to the bank.

questions.q: Name places in a city.
questions.a: Museum, library, shopping centre, cinema, hospital, town hall, bus station.

questions.q: How do we make suggestions about social activities?
questions.a: Let's go to the cinema. / How about meeting at the park? / Why don't we join a club?

units.name: Theme 6 - Life in the World & Culture

questions.q: How do we talk about countries and nationalities?
questions.a: Country + nationality: Turkey–Turkish, England–English, Japan–Japanese.

questions.q: What expressions are used to compare cultures?
questions.a: In my culture ... / Unlike in ... / Both ... and ... / whereas.

questions.q: Name some cultural elements.
questions.a: Traditional food, festivals, music, clothing, customs and celebrations.

units.name: Theme 7 - Life in Nature & Global Problems

questions.q: Name some global problems.
questions.a: Climate change, pollution, deforestation, water shortage, hunger, poverty.

questions.q: How do we express obligation and advice about the environment?
questions.a: We must reduce waste. We should recycle. We shouldn't cut down trees.

questions.q: Name natural disasters and natural elements.
questions.a: Earthquake, flood, drought, storm; mountain, river, forest, ocean.

units.name: Theme 8 - Life in the Universe & the Future

questions.q: How do we talk about future plans and predictions?
questions.a: Be going to (plan): I am going to study medicine. Will (prediction/decision): I think people will live on Mars.

questions.q: Name space-related vocabulary.
questions.a: Universe, planet, satellite, astronaut, spaceship, galaxy, telescope.

questions.q: What might life in the future be like?
questions.a: People may use robots and smart homes; travel may be faster and cleaner thanks to technology.
